Before the workshop, we are asking for two specific kinds of contribution:
candidate problems for the BENQODHI benchmark database, and proposals for how to
structure the Day 2 round table and focus groups.

::: {.idea-actions}
[Propose a benchmark problem](https://github.com/ocadni/benqodhi/issues/new?template=benchmark-problem.yml){.primary-action}
[Propose a round-table structure](https://github.com/ocadni/benqodhi/issues/new?template=round-table.yml){.secondary-action}
[Read submitted contributions](https://github.com/ocadni/benqodhi/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Aworkshop-idea){.secondary-action}
:::

Contributions are collected as public GitHub Issues so participants can read,
compare and refine proposals before the workshop.

If GitHub is inconvenient, send your idea by email:
[JRC-F7-CONFERENCES@ec.europa.eu](mailto:JRC-F7-CONFERENCES@ec.europa.eu)

## 1. Candidate problems for the benchmark database

Use this route to propose an optimisation problem that could become part of the
BENQODHI benchmark database. The issue form asks for:

- the problem summary,
- the biological or health use case,
- the optimisation formulation,
- possible datasets, instances or generators,
- baselines and metrics,
- why the problem is a good benchmark,
- references, tools or contacts.

The proposal does not need to be complete. A clear partial proposal is useful if
it identifies what is known, what is missing and what should be discussed at the
workshop.

::: {.idea-actions}
[Open the problem template](https://github.com/ocadni/benqodhi/issues/new?template=benchmark-problem.yml){.primary-action}
[Example problem proposal](https://github.com/ocadni/benqodhi/issues/1){.secondary-action}
:::

## 2. Round-table and focus-group structure

Use this route to propose how the Day 2 round table or parallel focus groups
should be organised. The issue form asks for:

- the proposed format,
- topics, tables or discussion blocks,
- roles such as facilitator, rapporteur or moderator,
- expected outputs,
- timing and practical constraints,
- risks or open decisions.

Good proposals should help the workshop produce concrete outputs: candidate
benchmark priorities, common metadata, dataset and repository needs, evaluation
metrics, and follow-up actions.

::: {.idea-actions}
[Open the round-table template](https://github.com/ocadni/benqodhi/issues/new?template=round-table.yml){.primary-action}
[Example round-table proposal](https://github.com/ocadni/benqodhi/issues/2){.secondary-action}
:::

## Example contributions

::: {.example-ideas}
::: {.example-idea}
### Haplotype phasing as a benchmark problem

Haplotype phasing is a concrete genomics optimization problem that could be discussed
as a BENQODHI benchmark. It has real sequencing use cases, known baselines, public
truth sets, and a natural route toward combinatorial formulations.
:::

::: {.example-idea}
### Day 2 round-table structure

The Day 2 session could combine parallel expert tables, rapporteur summaries and
a plenary consolidation step. Participants can suggest table themes, roles,
outputs, timing or a simpler format.
:::
:::
